checks_performed: Read the exact target and independently checked that the draft supplies the permitted counterexample-sequence alternative with the required ordered-triple normalization and asymptotic quantifiers.
Performed a complete parity-case proof of the population counts, mixed-parity correspondence, odd-odd count, total count, and density comparison.

Ran a persisted exact-integer checker that directly enumerates every ordered Schur triple for m=1,...,80, verifies the mixed-parity correspondence including multiplicity, and checks all stated formulas without floating-point arithmetic.

claims.claim: For n=22m, the stated coloring has 11m even color-1 elements, 5m odd color-2 elements, and 6m odd color-3 elements.
claims.evidence: Among 1,...,22m there are 11m evens. The color-2 odds comprise the 4m odds in [1,8m] and the m odds in (20m,22m], totaling 5m. The color-3 block contains the 6m odds in (8m,20m]. These disjoint classes exhaust [22m]. Exact enumeration confirmed the counts for m=1,...,80.
claims.search_method: Direct interval-and-parity counting, supplemented by exact integer enumeration for m=1,...,80.

claims.claim: Rainbow triples with one even and one odd addend are in two-to-one correspondence with pairs consisting of one color-2 odd and one color-3 odd.
claims.evidence: In a mixed-parity triple, the even addend e has color 1 and the sum z is odd. Thus the triple is rainbow exactly when its odd addend a and z have colors 2 and 3. Since z=a+e>a, it determines the cross-color odd pair {a,z}. Conversely, for any differently colored odds u<v, e=v-u is a positive even integer in [22m], and precisely (u,e,v) and (e,u,v) are the associated ordered triples. Different parity ensures the two orientations are distinct, and recovering {u,v} from the odd addend and sum proves uniqueness. The checker compared the full pair and triple sets and found multiplicity exactly two for m=1,...,80.
claims.search_method: Constructed and inverted the correspondence analytically; exhaustively compared its two finite sides using exact enumeration.

claims.claim: The number of mixed-parity ordered rainbow triples is 60m².
claims.evidence: There are (5m)(6m)=30m² pairs containing one color-2 odd and one color-3 odd. The verified correspondence gives exactly two ordered mixed-parity triples per pair, hence 60m². Direct enumeration matched this formula for every m from 1 through 80.
claims.search_method: Combined the proved population counts and correspondence, then checked the result by exact enumeration.

claims.claim: The number of odd-odd ordered rainbow triples is 39m²+3m.
claims.evidence: An odd-odd sum is even and has color 1, so the addends must have colors 2 and 3. A high color-2 odd is at least 20m+1, while a color-3 odd is at least 8m+1, making their sum exceed 22m. The remaining addends are 2i-1 (1≤i≤4m) and 8m+2j-1 (1≤j≤6m), with sum at most 22m exactly when i+j≤7m+1. The number of such unoriented cross-color pairs is 6m(m+1)+sum_{i=m+2}^{4m}(7m+1-i)=6m(m+1)+(3m-1)(9m)/2=(39m²+3m)/2. Their colors differ, so every pair has two distinct orientations, giving 39m²+3m. Exact enumeration confirmed this for m=1,...,80.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive parity/block case analysis and exact arithmetic counting of the admissible index region, supplemented by enumeration.

claims.claim: The coloring has exactly 99m²+3m ordered rainbow Schur triples.
claims.evidence: Mixed-parity and odd-odd addends contribute 60m² and 39m²+3m, respectively. Two even addends and their even sum all have color 1, so even-even triples contribute zero. These cases exhaust all addend parities, and their sum is 99m²+3m. The direct checker obtained exactly this total for m=1,...,80.
claims.search_method: Summed the proved exhaustive parity cases and independently enumerated all ordered Schur triples with exact integers.

claims.claim: This sequence has limiting rainbow density 9/22 and refutes the target with ε=1/220.
claims.evidence: There are binom(22m,2)=242m²-11m ordered Schur triples, so the density is (99m+3)/(242m-11), which tends to 99/242=9/22. Moreover, 22(99m+3)-9(242m-11)=165>0, so every member has density strictly above 9/22=90/220. For ε=1/220 the proposed bound is 2/5+1/220=89/220. Hence every n=22m violates it. Given any N, choosing m with 22m≥N supplies a violating coloring, so no eventual bound exists. The checker verified the corresponding integer cross-multiplications and all enumerated instances without division or floating point.
claims.search_method: Exact rational comparison by integer cross-multiplication, leading-coefficient limit calculation, and explicit verification of the negated asymptotic quantifiers.

target_evidence: The draft fully resolves the exact target through its allowed counterexample alternative. For the fixed positive ε=1/220, it constructs a valid 3-coloring for every n=22m and proves its ordered-rainbow-triple density exceeds 9/22=90/220>89/220=2/5+ε. Multiples 22m are unbounded, so for every proposed threshold N there is an n≥N violating the requested universal upper bound. The normalization is exactly by binom(n,2) ordered Schur triples, as required. Thus the counterexample has the requested strength, the headline that the proposed upper bound is false is established, and the draft's claimed_resolution of FULL is ACCURATE.
